limitations: TMSI is a terrain-morphology index, not a probability, habitability score, or safety certification.
Features are interpreted at a common physical scale of 20 m; no raster upsampling was performed.
Earth and planetary environmental conditions remain physically different even when morphology distributions are similar.

Earth DEM source data has approximately 29.3 m native resolution and was resampled to a 20 m processing grid; the resampling does not create additional observational detail. Effective measurement resolution remains constrained by the ~29.3 m source data.

Vertical datum difference: Earth uses NAVD88; Moon uses LOLA project datum; Mars uses delta geoid (MOLA control). Vertical datum differences are unquantified and may affect elevation-based feature comparisons (slope, local relief, terrain ruggedness).

Earth coverage is limited to two USGS 3DEP tiles (Death Valley / southern Arizona region, approximately 35°N–37°N, 116°W–117°W). These samples cannot establish global terrestrial terrain representativeness; results apply only to the sampled regions.
